items.q: What bottleneck is Achim actually talking about?
items.a: **Human verification.** Brilliant idea → written proof → peer trust cannot keep up when AI emits thousands of attacks on Riemann / Navier–Stokes / P vs NP. Only a couple thousand qualified reviewers have day jobs. Wiles and Perelman already showed **one writer, years of checkers**.

items.q: How fast did contest-math AI move?
items.a: ~2 years from brittle high-school contest AI to **2025 IMO-level** purported solutions. Automated systems solving **5/6 IMO** problems with **machine-checkable** proofs — gold-medal level with **no human review**.

items.q: What is the formal-math upgrade path?
items.a: Leibniz's trinity, now real: language (**Lean**), encyclopedia (**Mathlib**, ~**2M** lines), engine (**AI writing Lean**). A compiler check replaces multi-year mobilization. Humans keep questions and conjectures; computers **certify arrival**.

items.q: What is the fork if we refuse?
items.a: Humans stay the bottleneck and bake **internet + RLHF biases** into discovery engines. Adopt the partnership → **mathematical superintelligence** elevates humans to explorers and question-askers, not sole checkers.
